title: Act on the Prevention of and Countermeasures against School Violence
full_text:
Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Act is to protect students' human rights and foster their development as sound members of society by providing for matters necessary for the prevention of and countermeasures against school violence, thereby protecting victim students, guiding and educating aggressor students, and mediating disputes between victim students and aggressor students.

Article 2 (Definitions)
The terms used in this Act are defined as follows. <Amended 2009.5.8, 2012.1.26, 2012.3.21, 2021.3.23, 2023.10.24, 2025.1.31>
1. "School violence" means conduct occurring inside or outside school against a student that causes physical, mental or property damage through injury, assault, confinement, intimidation, abduction or enticement, defamation or insult, extortion, coercion or forced errands, sexual violence, ostracism, cyberviolence or similar acts.
1-2. "Ostracism" means any conduct whereby two or more students inside or outside school continuously or repeatedly attack a particular person or group of students physically or psychologically, causing that person or group to suffer.
1-3. "Cyberviolence" means ostracism against students using an information and communications network (meaning an information and communications network under subparagraph 1 of Article 2(1) of the Act on Promotion of Information and Communications Network Utilization and Information Protection, Etc.), the production or distribution of deepfake videos and the like (meaning photographs, videos or audio recordings in which a student's face, body or voice is edited, synthesized or processed using artificial intelligence technology or similar means into a form capable of arousing sexual desire or displeasure), and other conduct that causes physical, mental or property damage.
2. "School" means an elementary school, middle school, high school, special school or miscellaneous school under Article 2 of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act, or a school operated under Article 61 of that Act.
3. "Aggressor student" means a student, among the perpetrators, who commits school violence or participates in that conduct.
4. "Victim student" means a student who has suffered harm from school violence.
5. "Student with a disability" means a student who needs the special education provided for in Article 15 of the Act on Special Education for Persons with Disabilities, Etc. because of a physical, mental, intellectual or other disability.

Article 3 (Duty of Care in Interpretation and Application)
In interpreting and applying this Act, care shall be taken to ensure that the rights of the people are not unjustly infringed. <Amended 2021.3.23>

Article 4 (Responsibilities of the State and Local Governments)
① The State and local governments shall establish necessary legal and institutional arrangements, including investigation, research, education and public guidance, to prevent and eradicate school violence.
② The State and local governments shall encourage voluntary activities by the private sector, including youth-related organizations, to prevent school violence, protect victim students, and guide and educate aggressor students.
③ The State and local governments shall endeavor to reflect suggestions made by the private sector, including youth-related organizations under paragraph ②, in relevant policies.
④ The State and local governments shall provide the administrative and financial support necessary to discharge their responsibilities under paragraphs ① through ③. <Amended 2012.3.21>

Article 5 (Relationship to Other Acts)
① This Act applies to the regulation of school violence, protection of victim students and measures against aggressor students, except where another Act provides otherwise. <Amended 2021.3.23>
② This Act does not apply to sexual violence referred to in subparagraph 1 of Article 2 where another Act provides for such violence.

Article 6 (Establishment of Master Plans, Etc.)
① To achieve the purpose of this Act effectively, the Minister of Education shall set policy objectives and directions for the prevention of and countermeasures against school violence and, following deliberation by the Committee on Countermeasures against School Violence under Article 7, establish and implement a corresponding master plan for the prevention of and countermeasures against school violence (hereinafter referred to as the "master plan"). <Amended 2012.3.21, 2013.3.23>
② A master plan shall be established every five years and include the following matters. In such cases, the Minister of Education shall hear the opinions of relevant central administrative agencies and the superintendents of education (hereinafter referred to as "superintendents") of the Special Metropolitan City, Metropolitan Cities, Special Self-Governing Cities, Provinces and Special Self-Governing Provinces (hereinafter referred to as "Cities/Provinces"), and other relevant persons. <Amended 2012.3.21, 2013.3.23, 2025.1.21>
1. Investigation, research, education and public guidance for eradicating school violence;
2. Support for the treatment and rehabilitation of victim students;
3. Cooperation and support among administrative agencies and educational institutions concerned with school violence;
4. Assignment of professional counseling teachers under Article 14(1), and administrative and financial support therefor;
5. Administrative and financial support for youth-related organizations that prevent school violence and treat and educate victim students and aggressor students (hereinafter referred to as "specialized organizations"), or for experts;
6. Other matters necessary for the prevention of and countermeasures against school violence.
③ Each superintendent shall establish and implement an annual City/Province implementation plan for the prevention of and countermeasures against school violence (hereinafter referred to as an "implementation plan"), taking account of local conditions, including the contents of the master plan and the results of surveys on school violence under Article 11(8). <Added 2025.1.21>
④ Each superintendent shall annually publish the performance achieved under the previous year's implementation plan and the following year's implementation plan, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Added 2025.1.21>
⑤ The Minister of Education shall develop and distribute guidance on handling school violence cases, preventive education and related matters so that schools can respond effectively to school violence. <Added 2023.10.24, 2025.1.21>
⑥ The Minister of Education shall evaluate and publish the school violence prevention and countermeasures undertaken by City/Province offices of education and their performance, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Added 2012.1.26, 2013.3.23, 2023.10.24, 2025.1.21>
⑦ Other matters necessary for the establishment and implementation of master plans and implementation plans shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Added 2025.1.21>

Article 6-2 (Operation of Specialized Educational Institutions and Centers for Responding to School Violence, Etc.)
① The State may establish and operate specialized educational institutions to operate protective facilities for students' healing and recovery and to conduct research, education and related activities.
② The State may designate and operate centers for the effective prevention of and response to school violence (hereinafter referred to as "school violence prevention centers").
③ Matters concerning the establishment and operation of specialized educational institutions under paragraph ① and the designation and operation of school violence prevention centers under paragraph ② shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 7 (Establishment and Functions of the Committee on Countermeasures against School Violence)
A Committee on Countermeasures against School Violence (hereinafter referred to as the "Countermeasures Committee") shall be established under the Prime Minister to deliberate on the following matters concerning the prevention of and countermeasures against school violence. <Amended 2012.3.21, 2019.8.20>
1. Evaluation of the establishment and implementation of the master plan for the prevention of and countermeasures against school violence;
2. Matters requested by the heads of relevant central administrative agencies and local governments in connection with school violence;
3. Matters requested in connection with school violence by offices of education, Regional Committees on Countermeasures against School Violence under Article 9, Regional Consultative Councils on Countermeasures against School Violence under Article 10-2, Committees for Deliberation on Countermeasures against School Violence under Article 12, specialized organizations and experts.

Article 8 (Composition of the Countermeasures Committee)
① The Countermeasures Committee shall consist of no more than 20 members, including two chairpersons.
② The Prime Minister and a person commissioned by the President from among experts with extensive expertise and experience in school violence countermeasures shall serve jointly as chairpersons. Where both chairpersons are unable to perform their duties for unavoidable reasons, a member designated by the Prime Minister shall act on their behalf.
③ Members shall be persons commissioned by the President from among the following persons; provided that the persons under subparagraph 1 shall be ex officio members. <Amended 2013.3.23, 2014.11.19, 2017.7.26, 2025.10.1>
1. The Minister of Finance and Economy, Minister of Science and ICT, Minister of Education, Minister of Justice, Minister of the Interior and Safety, Minister of Culture, Sports and Tourism, Minister of Health and Welfare, Minister of Gender Equality and Family, Minister of Planning and Budget, Chairperson of the Broadcasting, Media and Communications Commission, and Commissioner General of the Korean National Police Agency;
2. Persons, one recommended by each member under subparagraph 1, from among experts with extensive expertise and experience in school violence countermeasures;
3. Grade III public officials or members of the Senior Civil Service belonging to relevant central administrative agencies and responsible for youth or medical affairs;
4. Persons who hold or have held a position of at least assistant professor or an equivalent position at a university or an accredited research institution, with expertise in school violence and related counseling or psychology;
5. Judges, prosecutors and attorneys-at-law;
6. Persons who have specialized in youth protection activities at a specialized organization for at least five years;
7. Persons qualified as medical doctors;
8. Parents with extensive experience in school steering committee activities and youth protection activities.
④ Members, including the chairpersons, shall serve a term of two years and may be reappointed for one further term only. <Amended 2021.3.23>
⑤ There shall be one executive secretary for the efficient operation and support of the Committee, and the Minister of Education shall serve as executive secretary. <Amended 2013.3.23>
⑥ A Working Committee on Countermeasures against School Violence (hereinafter referred to as the "Working Committee") shall be established within the Countermeasures Committee to assist its deliberations, including preliminary examination of matters to be submitted to it, and to deliberate on matters delegated by it.
⑦ Other matters necessary for the operation of the Countermeasures Committee and the composition and operation of the Working Committee shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 9 (Establishment of Regional Committees on Countermeasures against School Violence)
① A Regional Committee on Countermeasures against School Violence (hereinafter referred to as a "Regional Committee") shall be established in each City/Province to resolve local school violence issues. <Amended 2012.1.26>
② The Special Metropolitan City Mayor, Metropolitan City Mayors, Special Self-Governing City Mayors, Provincial Governors and Special Self-Governing Province Governors shall consult with the superintendent on the operation and activities of the Regional Committee and may establish a working committee for its efficient operation. <Amended 2012.1.26, 2025.1.21>
③ A Regional Committee shall consist of no more than 11 members, including one chairperson.
④ Matters necessary for the composition and operation of Regional Committees and working committees under paragraph ② shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 10 (Functions of Regional Committees on Countermeasures against School Violence, Etc.)
① Each Regional Committee shall establish annual measures for preventing school violence in its region (hereinafter referred to as "preventive measures") in accordance with the master plan. In such cases, the preventive measures shall include the contents of the implementation plan. <Amended 2025.1.21>
② Each Regional Committee shall annually submit to the Minister of Education the performance achieved under the previous year's preventive measures and the following year's preventive measures, as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Added 2025.1.21>
③ Other matters necessary for the establishment and implementation of preventive measures shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Added 2025.1.21>
④ A Regional Committee may request relevant materials from the superintendent and the Commissioner of the City/Province Police Agency concerning school violence occurring in its region. <Amended 2020.12.22, 2025.1.21>
⑤ Each superintendent shall, after hearing the opinions of the Regional Committee, designate institutions responsible for the counseling, treatment and education under subparagraphs 1 through 3 of Article 16(1) or subparagraph 5 of Article 17(1). <Amended 2012.1.26, 2025.1.21>
⑥ Upon designating an institution for counseling, treatment or education under paragraph ⑤, the superintendent shall post its name, location and functions on the website and endeavor to inform parents through various other means. <Added 2012.1.26, 2025.1.21>

Article 10-2 (Establishment and Operation of Regional Consultative Councils on Countermeasures against School Violence)
① A Regional Consultative Council on Countermeasures against School Violence (hereinafter referred to as a "Regional Consultative Council") shall be established in each Si/Gun/Gu to establish school violence prevention measures and discuss implementation plans for individual institutions and arrangements for mutual cooperation and support.
② A Regional Consultative Council shall consist of approximately 20 members, including one chairperson.
③ Other matters necessary for the composition and operation of Regional Consultative Councils shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 11 (Duties of Superintendents)
① Each superintendent shall establish and operate a dedicated department in the City/Province office of education responsible for integrated support, including prevention of and countermeasures against school violence and legal support. <Amended 2023.10.24>
② Where school violence occurs within the superintendent's jurisdiction, the superintendent may require the principal of the school concerned and principals of related schools to report its progress and outcome.
③ Where school violence within the superintendent's jurisdiction is connected with school violence outside that jurisdiction, the superintendent shall consult with the superintendent having jurisdiction and take appropriate measures.
④ Each superintendent shall require school principals to establish and implement execution plans for the prevention of and countermeasures against school violence.
⑤ No superintendent shall use the frequency of school violence in a school whose cases have been handled by a deliberation committee under Article 12 as adverse material in evaluating the principal's performance. <Amended 2019.8.20>
⑥ In the case of a transfer under subparagraph 8 of Article 17(1), the superintendent shall take the measures necessary to effect it; in the case of expulsion under subparagraph 9 of Article 17(1), the superintendent shall devise appropriate arrangements, including readmission to another school, for the student's sound development. <Amended 2012.1.26, 2012.3.21>
⑦ Each superintendent shall report to the Countermeasures Committee and the Regional Committee, and publish, matters concerning the actual state of school violence and countermeasures within the jurisdiction. The same shall apply to matters concerning school violence outside the jurisdiction that relate to a school within the jurisdiction. <Amended 2012.1.26, 2012.3.21>
⑧ Each superintendent shall conduct surveys on school violence at least twice a year to ascertain its actual state and establish effective preventive measures, and shall publish the results within 120 days after completion of each survey. <Added 2012.3.21, 2015.12.22, 2025.11.11>
⑨ Each superintendent shall establish and operate specialized institutions for investigations and counseling concerning school violence, operation of healing programs and protective facilities for students' healing and recovery, and integrated support including legal support. <Added 2012.3.21, 2023.10.24>
⑩ Each superintendent may provide education and other activities to improve the school violence expertise of members of dedicated bodies under Article 14(3). <Added 2023.10.24>
⑪ Where, following school violence within the jurisdiction, a principal or a teacher of the school attempts to minimize or conceal it when reporting its progress and outcome, the superintendent shall request a disciplinary resolution from the disciplinary committees under Article 50 of the Educational Officials Act and Article 62 of the Private School Act. <Added 2012.3.21, 2021.3.23, 2023.10.24>
⑫ Each superintendent may confer honors and awards on schools or their teachers that have made substantial contributions to preventing school violence and devising countermeasures within the jurisdiction, or award additional points in teachers' performance evaluations. <Added 2012.3.21, 2023.10.24>
⑬ Each superintendent shall provide education on the prevention of and countermeasures against school violence for principals and vice-principals at least once a year. <Added 2023.10.24>
⑭ Matters necessary for the composition of the dedicated department under paragraph ①, conduct of surveys on school violence under paragraph ⑧, establishment of specialized institutions under paragraph ⑨, and provision of education under paragraph ⑬ shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended 2012.3.21, 2023.10.24>

Article 11-2 (Investigation and Counseling on School Violence, Etc.)
① Each superintendent may perform the following investigations, counseling and related activities to prevent school violence and take follow-up measures. <Amended 2021.3.23>
1. Counseling of victim students and investigation of aggressor students;
2. Investigation of parents of aggressor students, where necessary;
3. Guidance on implementing plans for the prevention of and countermeasures against school violence;
4. Control of school violence gangs within the jurisdiction;
5. Entry into and inspection of private institutions and business establishments to prevent school violence;
6. Other matters necessary in connection with school violence and the like.
② A superintendent may entrust the investigations, counseling and related functions under paragraph ① to institutions or organizations prescribed by Presidential Decree.
③ Where necessary to perform the investigations, counseling and related functions under paragraph ①, the superintendent and the head of an entrusted institution or organization under paragraph ② may request cooperation from the heads of relevant institutions. <Amended 2021.3.23>
④ Where necessary for investigations, counseling and related activities under paragraph ①, a superintendent and a district superintendent of education to whom the superintendent's powers are delegated under Article 26(1) of the Local Education Autonomy Act may designate relevant staff to perform investigation and counseling duties, or commission and engage experts with extensive knowledge and experience in investigation and counseling as school violence investigators and counselors. They may have those staff and commissioned investigators and counselors conduct on-site investigations, inspect documents and perform similar activities, or request attendance, statements, cooperation in investigations and submission of materials from relevant persons, including victim students, aggressor students, student witnesses, relevant teachers and guardians. <Added 2025.1.21>
⑤ A superintendent or a district superintendent under paragraph ④ may provide administrative and financial support for the operation of school violence investigators and counselors. <Added 2025.1.21>
⑥ No person falling under any of the following subparagraphs may serve as a school violence investigator and counselor. <Added 2025.1.21>
1. A person falling under any subparagraph of Article 33 of the State Public Officials Act;
2. A person who committed a sexual offense against a child or youth under the Act on the Protection of Children and Youth against Sexual Abuse, a sexual crime under the Act on Special Cases concerning the Punishment, Etc. of Sexual Crimes, or a crime related to child abuse under the Child Welfare Act, and for whom ten years have not elapsed since the date a sentence of a fine became final, or since the date execution of a sentence of imprisonment without labor or heavier punishment, or medical treatment and custody, was completed, suspended or remitted.
⑦ To determine whether a person proposed for commissioning as a school violence investigator and counselor is subject to disqualification under paragraph ⑥, the superintendent or district superintendent under paragraph ④ shall, with that person's consent, request a criminal history check from the head of the relevant institution; provided that, where the proposed investigator and counselor directly submits a criminal history check reply to the superintendent or district superintendent, the criminal history check shall be deemed to have been conducted. <Added 2025.1.21>
⑧ The head of a relevant institution requested to conduct a criminal history check under paragraph ⑦ shall comply unless there is a justifiable reason not to do so. <Added 2025.1.21>
⑨ Relevant staff and school violence investigators and counselors conducting investigations, counseling and related activities under paragraphs ① and ④ shall carry identification indicating their authority and present it to the persons concerned. <Amended 2025.1.21>
⑩ The results of investigations and related activities under subparagraphs 1 and 4 of paragraph ① shall be notified to the school principal and guardians. <Amended 2025.1.21>
⑪ Other matters concerning the commissioning and operation of school violence investigators and counselors shall be determined by the superintendent. <Added 2025.1.21>

Article 11-3 (Cooperation with Relevant Institutions, Etc.)
① The Minister of Education, superintendents, district superintendents of education and school principals may request personal information and other information concerning school violence from the Commissioner General of the Korean National Police Agency, Commissioners of City/Province Police Agencies, chiefs of competent police stations and heads of relevant institutions. <Amended 2013.3.23, 2020.12.22>
② The Commissioner General of the Korean National Police Agency, Commissioners of City/Province Police Agencies, chiefs of competent police stations and heads of relevant institutions requested to provide information under paragraph ① shall comply unless there are special circumstances. <Amended 2020.12.22, 2021.3.23>
③ Matters necessary for cooperation with relevant institutions and the procedures therefor under paragraphs ① and ② shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
Article 11-4 (Support for and Exemption from Liability of Persons Responsible for School Violence Duties)
① School principals shall take necessary measures, including adjusting teaching hours, to support the activities of the responsible teachers under Article 14(3).
② To support teachers performing school violence prevention and response duties, the Minister of Education and superintendents may, through legal support teams under Article 14-2 of the Special Act on the Improvement of Teachers' Status and the Protection of Their Educational Activities, provide necessary legal services, including counseling concerning school violence and counseling where such teachers face civil litigation or criminal complaints or accusations.
③ Where principals and teachers provide student guidance for the prevention of and response to school violence under the Elementary and Secondary Education Act and other relevant statutes, they shall bear no civil or criminal liability arising from that guidance if it constitutes legitimate handling of a school violence case or legitimate student guidance conducted in compliance with relevant statutes and school regulations.

Article 12 (Establishment and Functions of Committees for Deliberation on Countermeasures against School Violence)
① A Committee for Deliberation on Countermeasures against School Violence (hereinafter referred to as a "Deliberation Committee") shall be established in each district office of education under Article 34 of the Local Education Autonomy Act and Article 80 of the Special Act on the Establishment of Jeju Special Self-Governing Province and the Development of Free International City (where there is no district office of education, an institution prescribed by ordinance of the City/Province concerned; hereinafter the same shall apply) to deliberate on matters concerning the prevention of and countermeasures against school violence; provided that, where grounds prescribed by Presidential Decree exist concerning its composition, two or more district offices of education may jointly constitute a Deliberation Committee after reporting to the superintendent. <Amended 2012.1.26, 2019.8.20>
② A Deliberation Committee shall deliberate on the following matters for the prevention of and countermeasures against school violence. <Amended 2012.1.26, 2019.8.20>
1. Prevention of and countermeasures against school violence;
2. Protection of victim students;
3. Education, guidance and discipline of aggressor students;
4. Mediation of disputes between victim students and aggressor students;
5. Other matters prescribed by Presidential Decree.
③ A Deliberation Committee may investigate school violence occurring in the relevant region and request relevant materials from school principals and the chief of the competent police station. <Added 2012.3.21, 2019.8.20>
④ Matters necessary for the establishment and functions of Deliberation Committees shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree, taking account of the size of the region and district office of education and other relevant circumstances. <Amended 2012.3.21, 2019.8.20>

Article 13 (Composition and Operation of Deliberation Committees)
① A Deliberation Committee shall consist of at least 10 and no more than 50 members, at least one-third of whom shall be commissioned from among parents of students attending schools (including high schools) within the jurisdiction of the relevant district office of education. <Amended 2019.8.20>
② The chairperson of a Deliberation Committee shall convene a meeting in any of the following cases. <Added 2011.5.19, 2012.1.26, 2012.3.21, 2019.8.20>
1. At least one-quarter of the members in office request a meeting;
2. A school principal requests a meeting;
3. A victim student or the student's guardian requests a meeting;
4. A report of the occurrence of school violence is received;
5. A report that an aggressor student has committed intimidation or retaliation is received;
6. The chairperson otherwise considers a meeting necessary.
③ A Deliberation Committee shall prepare and preserve minutes recording the date, time and place of meetings, members present, matters discussed, resolutions adopted and other relevant matters. <Added 2011.5.19, 2019.8.20>
④ Where a meeting is convened under paragraph ②, the district superintendent (where there is no district office of education, the head of the institution prescribed by ordinance of the City/Province concerned) shall notify the aggressor student, victim student and their guardians of the following matters. <Added 2024.1.9>
1. The date, time, place and agenda of the meeting;
2. The results of the meeting, including requests for measures.
⑤ During deliberations, a Deliberation Committee may have a pediatrician, psychiatrist, psychologist or other expert in child psychology attend, or hear their opinions in writing or by other means, and, where a victim student has received counseling or treatment, may hear the opinions of the relevant expert or specialist; provided that it shall ascertain the wishes of the victim student or the student's guardian and shall hear such opinions whenever the victim student or guardian so requests. <Added 2020.12.22, 2024.1.9>
⑥ Other matters necessary for the composition and operation of Deliberation Committees shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended 2011.5.19, 2019.8.20, 2020.12.22, 2024.1.9>

Article 13-2 (Resolution by School Principals)
① Notwithstanding subparagraphs 4 and 5 of Article 13(2), a school principal may resolve a minor school violence case that meets all of the following conditions internally where the victim student and the student's guardian do not wish a Deliberation Committee meeting to be held. In such cases, the principal shall report this to the Deliberation Committee without delay. <Amended 2021.3.23, 2023.10.24>
1. No medical certificate requiring at least two weeks of physical or mental treatment has been issued;
2. There is no property damage, or the property damage has been restored immediately or its restoration has been promised;
3. The school violence is not ongoing;
4. The conduct is not retaliation for reporting school violence, giving statements or providing materials, including retaliation using an information and communications network.
② A principal intending to resolve a case under paragraph ① shall complete all the following procedures.
1. Written confirmation of whether the victim student and the student's guardian wish a Deliberation Committee meeting to be held;
2. Written confirmation and deliberation by the dedicated body under Article 14(3) concerning the severity of the school violence.
③ Where the victim student and the student's guardian wish a Deliberation Committee meeting to be held for minor school violence under paragraph ①, the principal may recommend a program for restoring the relationship between the victim student and aggressor student (hereinafter referred to as a "relationship restoration program"). <Added 2023.10.24>
④ The State and local governments may provide administrative and financial support where necessary for developing, distributing and operating relationship restoration programs. <Added 2023.10.24>
⑤ Other matters necessary for the internal resolution of school violence by principals shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended 2023.10.24>

Article 14 (Assignment of Professional Counseling Teachers and Constitution of Dedicated Bodies)
① Each principal shall establish a counseling room at the school as prescribed by Presidential Decree and assign a professional counseling teacher under Article 19-2 of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act.
② When requested by the principal or Deliberation Committee, professional counseling teachers shall report the results of counseling with victim students and aggressor students involved in school violence. <Amended 2019.8.20>
③ Each principal shall constitute a body dedicated to school violence issues (hereinafter referred to as a "dedicated body") consisting of the vice-principal, professional counseling teacher, school health teacher, responsible teacher (meaning the teacher responsible for school violence issues), parents and other relevant persons. In such cases, parents shall constitute at least one-third of its members. <Amended 2012.3.21, 2019.8.20>
④ Upon becoming aware of a school violence incident, the principal shall, without delay, have the dedicated body or teachers of the school ascertain whether the alleged perpetration and harm occurred, and have the dedicated body deliberate on whether to refer the case for internal resolution by the principal under Article 13-2. <Added 2019.8.20>
⑤ A dedicated body shall organize and conduct surveys on school violence (hereinafter referred to as "fact-finding surveys") and school violence prevention programs, and shall, when requested by the principal or Deliberation Committee, report the results of its activities, including school violence investigations. <Amended 2012.3.21, 2019.8.20>
⑥ A victim student or the student's guardian may request a fact-finding survey from the dedicated body to ascertain the facts of the harm. <Added 2009.5.8, 2012.3.21, 2019.8.20>
⑦ The State and local governments shall provide budgetary support for fact-finding surveys, relevant administrative agencies shall cooperate with them, and principals may provide administrative and financial support to dedicated bodies. <Amended 2009.5.8, 2012.3.21, 2019.8.20>
⑧ Where necessary to secure expertise in fact-finding surveys concerning particular school violence cases, including sexual violence, a dedicated body may commission a specialized institution to conduct the survey. In such cases, the commission shall be made in the principal's name after deliberation by the chairperson of the Deliberation Committee. <Added 2012.1.26, 2012.3.21, 2019.8.20>
⑨ Other matters necessary for the operation of dedicated bodies shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Added 2012.3.21, 2019.8.20>

Article 15 (School Violence Prevention Education, Etc.)
① Principals shall provide students with education for their physical and mental protection and prevention of school violence (which shall include the concept and actual state of school violence and ways of responding to it) at least once each semester. <Amended 2012.1.26>
② Principals shall provide school personnel and parents with education on the prevention of and countermeasures against school violence at least once each semester. <Amended 2012.3.21>
③ To prevent school violence, principals may determine and operate necessary arrangements enabling teachers, students, parents and other school community members to recognize and fulfill their responsibilities concerning school violence. <Added 2023.10.24>
④ In consultation with the dedicated body, principals may entrust the design and operation of school violence prevention education programs under paragraph ① to specialized organizations or experts. <Amended 2023.10.24>
⑤ District superintendents shall endeavor to publicize to parents, through mobile phone text messages, website postings and various other means, the design and operating plans of school violence prevention education programs under paragraphs ①, ② and ④, so that parents can easily access them and participation is encouraged. <Amended 2012.1.26, 2023.10.24>
⑥ The Minister of Education may produce promotional videos on the prevention of and countermeasures against school violence, distribute them to broadcasting business operators under subparagraph 3 of Article 2 of the Broadcasting Act, and request their broadcast. <Added 2023.10.24>
⑦ Other matters concerning the provision of school violence prevention education shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended 2011.5.19, 2023.10.24>

Article 15-2 (Designation and Observance of School Violence Prevention Day)
① To foster a sound school life culture and raise awareness of school violence, the fourth Monday of May each year shall be School Violence Prevention Day, and the week beginning on that day shall be School Violence Prevention Week.
② The State and local governments shall endeavor to conduct events, education and publicity consistent with the purpose of School Violence Prevention Day.

Article 16 (Protection of Victim Students)
① Where a Deliberation Committee deems it necessary to protect a victim student, it may request the district superintendent (where there is none, the head of the institution prescribed by ordinance under Article 12(1); hereinafter the same shall apply) to take any of the following measures for that student, including imposing several measures simultaneously; provided that, upon becoming aware of a school violence case, the principal shall separate the perpetrator (including a teacher) from the victim student without delay unless special circumstances prescribed by Presidential Decree exist, such as the victim student's opposition. Where the victim student requests emergency protection, the principal may take the measures under subparagraphs 1 through 3 and 6. In such cases, the principal shall immediately report to the Deliberation Committee. <Amended 2012.3.21, 2017.4.18, 2019.8.20, 2020.12.22, 2021.3.23, 2023.10.24>
1. Psychological counseling and advice by experts inside or outside school;
2. Temporary protection;
3. Medical treatment and recuperation for treatment;
4. Change of class;
5. Deleted <2012.3.21>
6. Other measures necessary to protect the victim student.
② Before requesting measures under paragraph ①, the Deliberation Committee shall follow appropriate procedures, including giving the victim student and the student's guardian an opportunity to state their opinions. <Added 2012.3.21, 2019.8.20>
③ Upon a request under paragraph ①, the district superintendent shall take the relevant measures within seven days with the consent of the victim student's guardian. <Amended 2012.3.21, 2019.8.20>
④ Where a principal so recognizes for a student requiring protection, including measures under paragraph ①, absences necessary for those measures may be counted as days of attendance. <Amended 2012.3.21, 2021.3.23>
⑤ In evaluating grades and other matters, principals shall endeavor to ensure that students are not disadvantaged by measures under paragraph ③. <Amended 2012.3.21, 2021.3.23>
⑥ The guardian of the aggressor student shall bear expenses incurred by the victim student in receiving counseling and related services under subparagraphs 1 through 3 of paragraph ① from specialized organizations or experts; provided that, where the principal or victim student's guardian so desires for the victim student's prompt treatment, the School Safety Mutual Aid Association under Article 15 of the Act on the Prevention of and Compensation for Accidents at School or the City/Province office of education may bear those expenses and exercise a right to reimbursement. <Amended 2012.1.26, 2012.3.21, 2021.3.23>
1. Deleted <2012.3.21>
2. Deleted <2012.3.21>
⑦ Where necessary, the principal or the victim student's guardian may directly claim the mutual aid benefits under Article 34 of the Act on the Prevention of and Compensation for Accidents at School from the School Safety Mutual Aid Association. <Added 2012.1.26, 2012.3.21>
⑧ Matters necessary for the protection of victim students and for the scope of support, scope of reimbursement claims and payment procedures under paragraph ⑥ shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Added 2012.3.21, 2021.3.23>

Article 16-2 (Protection of Students with Disabilities)
① No person shall commit school violence against a student with a disability on the grounds of disability or similar grounds.
② Where a victim student or aggressor student is a student with a disability, a Deliberation Committee may have a special education expert, such as special education teaching personnel under subparagraph 4 of Article 2 of the Act on Special Education for Persons with Disabilities, Etc., or a disability expert attend its deliberations, or hear their opinions in writing or by other means; provided that it shall ascertain the wishes of the student with a disability or the student's guardian and, where the student or guardian so requests, shall have a special education expert or disability expert attend the deliberations or hear their opinions in writing or by other means. <Added 2020.12.22, 2026.6.2>
③ To protect a student with a disability harmed by school violence, a Deliberation Committee may request the principal to arrange counseling by a counselor specializing in disabilities or recuperation at a treatment institution specializing in disabilities. <Amended 2019.8.20, 2020.12.22>
④ Upon a request under paragraph ③, the principal shall take the relevant measures. In such cases, Article 16(6) shall apply mutatis mutandis. <Amended 2012.3.21, 2020.12.22>

Article 16-3 (Victim Student Support Assistants)
① A superintendent or district superintendent may designate assistants who connect victim students with the services and support institutions they need for legal assistance, counseling, protection and other support (hereinafter referred to as "victim student support assistants").
② A superintendent or district superintendent shall provide administrative and financial support for the operation of victim student support assistants.
③ Matters concerning the designation and operation of victim student support assistants shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 16-4 (Support for Victims of Cyberviolence)
① The State may provide support for the deletion of photographs, videos, audio recordings, copies, edited materials, synthesized materials, processed materials, personal information, false statements and similar materials constituting cyberviolence (hereinafter referred to in this Article as "recordings, etc.") for students harmed by their distribution over an information and communications network (meaning harm suffered by being the subject of those recordings, etc.). <Amended 2025.1.31>
② A victim student under paragraph ①, the student's guardian, or a representative designated by the victim student or guardian (hereinafter referred to in this Article as an "applicant for deletion support") may request State support for deletion of recordings, etc. In such cases, the applicant shall request deletion support in compliance with the requirements prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended 2025.3.18>
③ Notwithstanding paragraph ②, for child or youth sexual exploitation materials under subparagraph 5 of Article 2 of the Act on the Protection of Children and Youth against Sexual Abuse, a superintendent or district superintendent may request the State and local governments to provide deletion support under Article 7-3(3) of the Sexual Violence Prevention and Victims Protection Act without a request from an applicant for deletion support. <Added 2025.3.18>
④ The aggressor student responsible for the cyberviolence or the student's guardian shall bear the costs of deletion support for recordings, etc. under paragraph ①. <Amended 2025.3.18>
⑤ Where the State has incurred costs of deletion support for recordings, etc. under paragraph ①, it may exercise a right to reimbursement against the aggressor student responsible for the cyberviolence or the student's guardian. <Amended 2025.3.18>
⑥ Matters necessary for the content and methods of deletion support for recordings, etc. under paragraphs ① and ②, and procedures and methods for exercising the right to reimbursement under paragraph ⑤, shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended 2025.3.18>

Article 17 (Measures against Aggressor Students)
① To protect victim students and guide and educate aggressor students, a Deliberation Committee shall request the district superintendent to take any of the following measures against an aggressor student, including imposing several measures simultaneously. The criteria for applying each measure shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree; provided that expulsion shall not apply to aggressor students in compulsory education. <Amended 2009.5.8, 2012.1.26, 2012.3.21, 2019.8.20, 2021.3.23, 2023.10.24>
1. Written apology to the victim student;
2. Prohibition of contact with, intimidation of, and retaliation against the victim student and students who reported or made accusations, including conduct using an information and communications network;
3. Service at school;
4. Community service;
5. Completion of special education or psychological treatment provided by experts inside or outside school or institutions designated by the superintendent;
6. Suspension of attendance;
7. Change of class;
8. Transfer to another school;
9. Expulsion.
② Where a Deliberation Committee requests measures against an aggressor student under paragraph ① on the grounds of intimidation or retaliation against a victim student or a student who reported or made accusations, including conduct using an information and communications network, it may impose measures under subparagraphs 6 through 9 of that paragraph simultaneously or intensify the measures. <Added 2012.3.21, 2019.8.20, 2021.3.23, 2023.10.24>
③ An aggressor student subjected to measures under subparagraphs 2 through 4 and 6 through 8 of paragraph ① shall complete special education or receive psychological treatment at an institution designated by the superintendent (including an alternative education institution), for a period determined by the Deliberation Committee. <Amended 2012.1.26, 2012.3.21, 2019.8.20, 2023.10.24>
④ Upon becoming aware of school violence, the principal shall take the measure under subparagraph 2 of paragraph ① without delay. <Added 2023.10.24>
⑤ Where the principal deems protection of the victim student and guidance and education of the aggressor student urgent, the principal may first impose the measures under subparagraphs 1, 3 and 5 through 7 of paragraph ① individually or simultaneously. In such cases, the principal shall immediately report to the Deliberation Committee and obtain its ratification. <Amended 2012.1.26, 2012.3.21, 2019.8.20, 2021.3.23, 2023.10.24>
⑥ At the request of the victim student and the student's guardian, the principal may take the measure under subparagraph 6 or 7 of paragraph ① following deliberation by the dedicated body. In such cases, the principal shall immediately report to the Deliberation Committee and obtain its ratification. <Added 2023.10.24>
⑦ The period of suspension of attendance under subparagraph 6 of paragraph ① imposed by the principal under paragraphs ⑤ and ⑥ may be set to last until the Deliberation Committee decides on measures. <Added 2023.10.24>
⑧ Before requesting measures under paragraph ① or ②, the Deliberation Committee shall follow appropriate procedures, including giving the aggressor student and guardian an opportunity to state their opinions. <Amended 2012.3.21, 2019.8.20, 2023.10.24>
⑨ Upon a request under paragraph ①, the district superintendent shall take the relevant measures within 14 days. <Amended 2012.1.26, 2012.3.21, 2019.8.20, 2023.10.24>
⑩ When a principal takes measures under paragraphs ④ through ⑥, the principal shall notify the aggressor student and the student's guardian. If the aggressor student refuses or evades them, the principal shall impose discipline under Article 18 of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act. <Amended 2012.3.21, 2019.8.20, 2023.10.24>
⑪ The guardian of an aggressor student subjected to the measure under subparagraph 2 of paragraph ① shall endeavor to ensure that the student appropriately complies with it. <Added 2023.10.24>
⑫ Where an aggressor student is subjected to measures under subparagraphs 3 through 5 of paragraph ①, associated absences may be counted as days of attendance if the principal so recognizes. <Amended 2012.1.26, 2012.3.21, 2021.3.23, 2023.10.24>
⑬ Where an aggressor student completes special education, the Deliberation Committee shall have the student's guardian also receive education with the student. If the victim student is a student with a disability, the education shall include disability awareness education. <Amended 2012.3.21, 2019.8.20, 2023.10.24>
⑭ After an aggressor student transfers to another school, the student shall be prevented from transferring back to the school attended by the victim student before that transfer. <Added 2012.1.26, 2012.3.21, 2023.10.24>
⑮ If a student subjected to measures under subparagraphs 2 through 9 of paragraph ① refuses or evades those measures, the Deliberation Committee may, notwithstanding paragraph ⑦, request the district superintendent to take additional different measures as prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Added 2012.3.21, 2019.8.20, 2023.10.24>
<16> If measures or discipline under paragraphs ⑨, ⑩ and ⑮ are delayed or not implemented, the victim student and the student's guardian may report this to the superintendent. Upon receiving a report, the superintendent shall investigate the district superintendent or principal without delay, as prescribed by Presidential Decree, to verify the facts. <Added 2024.1.9>
<17> Matters necessary for measures against aggressor students and readmission under Article 11(6) shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Added 2012.3.21, 2023.10.24, 2024.1.9>
Article 17-2 (Administrative Appeals)
① A victim student or the student's guardian who objects to measures taken by the district superintendent under Articles 16(1) and 17(1) may file an administrative appeal under the Administrative Appeals Act. <Added 2012.3.21, 2017.11.28, 2019.8.20>
② An aggressor student or the student's guardian who objects to measures taken by the district superintendent under Article 17(1) may file an administrative appeal under the Administrative Appeals Act. <Amended 2012.3.21, 2017.11.28, 2019.8.20>
③ The administrative appeals commission shall notify the victim student or the student's guardian and the schools attended by the victim and aggressor students that an administrative appeal under paragraph ② has been filed, and provide written guidance on intervention in the appeal under Article 20 of the Administrative Appeals Act. <Added 2023.10.24>
④ The Administrative Appeals Act shall apply mutatis mutandis to matters necessary for filing administrative appeals under paragraphs ① and ②. <Amended 2019.8.20, 2023.10.24>
⑤ Deleted <2019.8.20>
⑥ Deleted <2019.8.20>

Article 17-3 (Administrative Litigation)
① A victim student or the student's guardian who objects to measures taken by the district superintendent under Articles 16(1) and 17(1) may institute administrative litigation under the Administrative Litigation Act.
② An aggressor student or the student's guardian who objects to measures taken by the district superintendent under Article 17(1) may institute administrative litigation under the Administrative Litigation Act.
③ The district superintendent shall notify the victim and aggressor students or their guardians, and the schools attended by the victim and aggressor students, that administrative litigation under paragraphs ① and ② has been instituted, and provide written guidance on intervention in litigation under Article 16 of the Administrative Litigation Act.
④ The Administrative Litigation Act shall apply mutatis mutandis to matters necessary for instituting administrative litigation under paragraphs ① and ②.

Article 17-4 (Suspension of Execution)
① Where an administrative appeals commission or a court intends to order suspension of execution under Article 30 of the Administrative Appeals Act or Article 23 of the Administrative Litigation Act in respect of measures under Article 17(1), it shall hear the opinions of the victim student or the student's guardian; provided that it may dispense with hearing opinions where the victim student or guardian has clearly indicated a waiver of the opportunity to state opinions or in similar circumstances.
② Where a superintendent or district superintendent receives notification from an administrative appeals commission or court that an application for suspension of execution has been made and of its outcome, the superintendent or district superintendent shall notify the victim student or the student's guardian and the schools attended by the victim and aggressor students of that fact and outcome.
③ Where an application for suspension of execution of measures under Article 17(1) is granted, the victim student and the student's guardian may request the principal to separate the victim student from the aggressor student. The principal shall separate them following deliberation by the dedicated body.
④ Matters necessary for procedures, methods and exceptions for hearing opinions under paragraph ① shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree in cases of suspension of execution under Article 30 of the Administrative Appeals Act, and by Rules of the Supreme Court in cases of suspension of execution under Article 23 of the Administrative Litigation Act.

Article 17-5 (Time Limits for Trial)
Where an aggressor student or the student's guardian who objects to measures taken by the district superintendent under Article 17(1) institutes administrative litigation under the Administrative Litigation Act, trial of the administrative case shall be conducted expeditiously, with priority over other trials. Judgment shall be pronounced within 90 days after the action is instituted at first instance, and within 60 days after pronouncement of the preceding instance's judgment at each of the second and third instances.

Article 18 (Dispute Mediation)
① A Deliberation Committee may mediate a dispute concerning school violence. <Amended 2019.8.20>
② The period of dispute mediation under paragraph ① shall not exceed one month.
③ Dispute mediation concerning school violence shall include the following matters. <Amended 2019.8.20>
1. Mediation of agreements on compensation for damage between victim students and aggressor students or between their guardians;
2. Other matters deemed necessary by the Deliberation Committee.
④ Where necessary for dispute mediation, a Deliberation Committee may investigate matters concerning school violence with the cooperation of relevant institutions. <Amended 2019.8.20>
⑤ Where a Deliberation Committee intends to mediate a dispute, it shall notify the victim student, aggressor student and their guardians. <Amended 2019.8.20>
⑥ Where a dispute arises between students belonging to different district offices of education within the jurisdiction of a City/Province office of education, the superintendent shall mediate the dispute directly. In such cases, paragraphs ② through ⑤ shall apply mutatis mutandis. <Amended 2019.8.20>
⑦ Where a dispute arises between students attending schools under City/Province offices of education with different jurisdictions, the superintendent supervising the victim student shall mediate the dispute directly after consulting with the superintendent supervising the aggressor student. In such cases, paragraphs ② through ⑤ shall apply mutatis mutandis. <Amended 2019.8.20>

Article 19 (Duties of Principals)
① Principals shall cooperate in implementing measures under Articles 16, 16-2 and 17.
② No principal shall minimize or conceal school violence.
③ Principals shall report to the superintendent the occurrence of school violence, cases internally resolved by the principal under Article 13-2, measures under Articles 16, 16-2, 17 and 18 and their outcomes, and shall endeavor, in cooperation with relevant institutions, to prevent the formation of and disband school violence groups within schools.
④ Where necessary to prevent school violence, principals shall endeavor to detect and respond to it early, including investigating the situation of school violence at the school. <Added 2023.10.24>

Article 20 (Duty to Report School Violence)
① Any person who witnesses school violence or becomes aware of it shall immediately report it to a school or other relevant institution.
② An institution receiving a report under paragraph ① shall notify the guardians of the aggressor student and victim student and the principals of their schools. <Amended 2009.5.8>
③ A principal notified under paragraph ② shall notify the Deliberation Committee without delay. <Added 2009.5.8, 2019.8.20>
④ Any person who becomes aware of preparation or conspiracy to commit school violence or similar conduct may make an accusation to the principal or Deliberation Committee; provided that a teacher who becomes aware of it shall report to the principal and inform the relevant parents. <Amended 2009.5.8, 2012.1.26, 2019.8.20>
⑤ No person shall disadvantage a person who reports school violence under paragraphs ① through ④ on the grounds of making that report. <Added 2012.3.21>

Article 20-2 (Establishment of Emergency Telephone Lines, Etc.)
① The State and local governments shall establish emergency telephone lines to receive reports of school violence at any time and provide counseling on it.
② The State and local governments may entrust the establishment and operation of emergency telephone lines under paragraph ① to institutions or organizations prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Added 2012.1.26>
③ Matters necessary for the establishment, operation and entrustment of emergency telephone lines under paragraphs ① and ② shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree. <Amended 2012.1.26>

Article 20-3 Deleted <2023.10.24>

Article 20-4 (Use of Information and Communications Networks, Etc.)
① The State, local governments or superintendents may use information and communications networks where necessary to perform school violence prevention and related duties effectively.
② Where schools or students (including parents) perform school violence prevention and related duties using information and communications networks under paragraph ①, the State, local governments or superintendents may subsidize all or part of any of the following costs.
1. Costs incurred by schools or students (including parents) in purchasing or using telecommunications equipment;
2. Telecommunications service charges imposed on schools or students (including parents).
③ Other matters necessary for the use of information and communications networks shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 20-5 (Deployment of Student Protection Personnel, Etc.)
① The State, local governments or principals may deploy and utilize student protection personnel within schools to prevent school violence.
② No person falling under any of the following subparagraphs may serve as student protection personnel. <Added 2013.7.30, 2021.3.23>
1. A person falling under any subparagraph of Article 33 of the State Public Officials Act;
2. A person who committed a sexual offense against a child or youth under the Act on the Protection of Children and Youth against Sexual Abuse or a sexual crime under the Act on Special Cases concerning the Punishment, Etc. of Sexual Crimes, and for whom ten years have not elapsed since the date a sentence of a fine became final, or since the date execution of a sentence of imprisonment without labor or heavier punishment, or medical treatment and custody, was completed, suspended or remitted;
3. Owners or workers of establishments prohibited from admitting or employing juveniles under subitem 3 and subitems 7 through 9 of item (a) of subparagraph 5 of Article 2 of the Youth Protection Act.
③ The State, local governments or principals may entrust duties concerning the deployment and utilization of student protection personnel under paragraph ① to relevant specialized institutions or organizations. <Amended 2013.7.30>
④ A specialized institution or organization entrusted with duties concerning the deployment and utilization of student protection personnel under paragraph ③ shall consult sufficiently with the principal when performing those duties. <Amended 2013.7.30, 2021.3.23>
⑤ The State, local governments or principals may, with the consent of a person proposed for deployment as student protection personnel, request that person's criminal history from the Commissioner General of the Korean National Police Agency. <Added 2013.7.30>
⑥ A specialized institution or organization entrusted with duties concerning the deployment and utilization of student protection personnel under paragraph ③ may apply to the entrusting State authority, local government or principal for a criminal history check of a person proposed for deployment as student protection personnel. <Added 2013.7.30>
⑦ A person wishing to serve as student protection personnel shall submit to the State, local government or principal a written confirmation that the person does not fall under any subparagraph of paragraph ②. <Added 2013.7.30>

Article 20-6 (School Police Officers)
① The State may assign police officers dedicated to school violence and related duties to prevent and eradicate school violence.
② Matters necessary for the operation of school police officers under paragraph ① shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 20-7 (Integrated Monitoring of Video Information Processing Devices)
① To perform school violence prevention duties effectively, the State and local governments may, in consultation with the superintendent, integrate and monitor video information processing devices installed inside and outside schools (meaning fixed video information processing devices under subparagraph 7 of Article 2 of the Personal Information Protection Act; hereinafter the same shall apply in this Article). In such cases, they shall process only the minimum personal information necessary for integrated monitoring and shall not use it for any other purpose. <Amended 2023.3.14>
② The State and local governments intending to integrate and monitor video information processing devices under paragraph ① shall collect the opinions of relevant experts and interested parties through procedures prescribed by Presidential Decree, including public hearings and briefing sessions.
③ Where video information processing devices installed inside and outside a school are integrated and monitored under paragraph ①, the operator of the school's video information processing devices shall inform data subjects of that fact through the measures under Article 25(4) of the Personal Information Protection Act.
④ Except as provided in this Act, the Personal Information Protection Act shall apply to integrated monitoring.
⑤ Other matters necessary for integrated monitoring of video information processing devices shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 21 (Prohibition of Divulging Confidential Information, Etc.)
① No person who performs or has performed duties concerning the prevention of and countermeasures against school violence under this Act shall divulge confidential information learned in the course of those duties or materials concerning aggressor students, victim students, and persons who report or make accusations under Article 20. <Amended 2012.1.26, 2021.3.23>
② The specific scope of confidential information under paragraph ① shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
③ Meetings of Deliberation Committees under Articles 16, 16-2, 17, 17-2 and 18 shall not be open to the public; provided that, where a victim student, aggressor student or their guardian applies for disclosure of minutes, including inspection or copying, the minutes shall be disclosed with personal information excluded, including names, resident registration numbers and addresses of the students and their family members, and names of committee members. <Amended 2011.5.19, 2012.3.21, 2019.8.20>

Article 21-2 (Special Provisions concerning the Local Education Autonomy Act)
Notwithstanding Article 35 of the Local Education Autonomy Act, a district superintendent may be delegated to perform duties under this Act concerning protection of victim students of school violence at high schools, guidance and education of aggressor students, mediation of disputes between victim students and aggressor students, and related matters.

Article 22 (Penalty)
A person who violates Article 21(1) shall be punished by imprisonment with labor for not more than one year or a fine not exceeding KRW 10,000,000.

Article 23 (Administrative Fines)
① An administrative fine not exceeding KRW 3,000,000 shall be imposed on a guardian who fails to comply with a Deliberation Committee's measure requiring completion of education under Article 17(13). <Amended 2019.8.20, 2023.10.24>
② Administrative fines under paragraph ① shall be imposed and collected by the superintendent as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
